card.name: Punctuation in scholarly encyclopedic prose
card.fires_on: Sentence-ending periods and commas, plus occasional linking words like "sometimes" or "with", in academic or encyclopedia-style general text (history, philosophy, physics, religion). Commas after dates in biographical entries also count.

modes.label: Sentence-ending period
modes.description: A period closing a declarative sentence in an analytical or historical passage.
modes.example: Hence a sufficiently uniform motion will be indistinguishable from rest<<. >>Leibniz, later, articulated

modes.label: Comma after a date
modes.description: A comma following a day or month in a biographical date.
modes.example: died at Madrid, 27 March<<,>> 1625. He was

modes.label: Mid-clause connector
modes.description: An adverb or preposition inside a clause that leads into an explanation or contrast.
modes.example: where it<< sometimes>> translates the Hebrew word for assembly, k
